title: Project P.I.T.T.
genre: Physics sandbox / automation-factory / incremental-idle (mass-produce rubber ducks and feed them to a pit, 'The Maw')
release_date: 2026-08-19 (Steam, PC; Kotaku lists 08-18, a time-zone difference) [CONFIRMED – Pirate PR press release / Steam store / TechTimes / Automaton]
early_access_date: n/a (released as 1.0; earlier free itch.io version/demo and a Steam demo, app 4636730)
team_size: 1 (solo) [CONFIRMED – Automaton 2026-08-25, citing the dev's own Reddit retrospective: first game, made alone; DLCompare: 'mostly developed by the independent developer Froke']
country: France [per press: described as a 'French solo developer' (French-language coverage via DLCompare.fr / GoCleCD); not stated by the dev in sources seen]
developer_background: First game, made alone in about 1 year [CONFIRMED – dev's Reddit post via Automaton]. Began as a small experiment inspired by incremental and automation games; early prototypes used plain spheres that rolled too regularly, so Froke swapped them for rubber ducks (DLCompare.fr). Released a free itch.io version first, which went viral on YouTube, then signed with publisher Pretty Soon for Steam.
publisher: Pretty Soon [Steam store / press release]; Green Man Gaming lists Plug-in Digital (probably distributor). Dev/publisher revenue split undisclosed.
platforms_and_store_links: Steam: https://store.steampowered.com/app/4026250/Project_PITT/ ; Steam demo: https://store.steampowered.com/app/4636730/Project_PITT_Demo/ ; itch.io demo: https://fr0ke.itch.io/project-pitt-demo ; Steam Deck Verified (SDHQ disputes it for late-game performance)
business_model: Premium $9.99 [CONFIRMED – Steam store]; 15% launch discount through 2026-09-02 [TechTimes]; later 20% off ($7.99) and a 'Project P.I.T.T. x Sort Them Ducks' bundle (~$12.04) [Steam store / gg.deals]. Free demo on Steam and itch.io.
units_or_downloads: 22,000+ copies in the first 24 hours and 50,000+ by ~2026-08-24 [CONFIRMED – dev (Reddit retrospective via Automaton; DLCompare)]. ~60,000–75,000 by 2026-10-08 [ESTIMATE – ~1,000–1,050 reviews × 60 (cheap, YouTube-viral; implied ratio ≥50 from dev data)]. Raijin's earlier ~22,300 estimate (medium confidence) is far below the dev's figure and is disregarded. itch.io free version: 65,000+ downloads [UNVERIFIED – figure circulated with the launch PR; not found in the search snippets I could access].
peak_concurrent_players: ~3,900 all-time peak (launch week, Aug 2026) [CONFIRMED – dev retrospective via Automaton]; 3,928 in August 2026 [ESTIMATE – Raijin, as of 2026-09-07]. ~452 in-game on 2026-09-07; August average ~996 [Raijin].
steam_reviews: 92% positive 'Very Positive' on launch day → 78% 'Mostly Positive' by ~2026-08-25 [Automaton]; 920 @ 80% [Raijin, earlier]; 988 @ 79% [DLCompare.fr]; 1,000+ @ ~79% 'Mostly Positive' on ~2026-10-08 [Steam store snapshot].
implied_review_multiplier: n/a for an exact same-date pair; lower bound ≈ 50 (50,000 confirmed units by 2026-08-24 ÷ ~1,000 reviews by Oct 2026; there were fewer reviews on Aug 24, so the true ratio then was higher)
gross_revenue: $400,000+ gross by ~2026-08-24 (≈50k units) [CONFIRMED – dev via Automaton/DLCompare]. ~$450k–$560k by 2026-10-08 [ESTIMATE – 60k–75k units × $7.49 (list $9.99 × 0.75)]. Raijin's ~$187k (earlier, medium confidence) conflicts with dev data and is disregarded.
net_revenue: ~$290k–$365k to developer + publisher combined [ESTIMATE – gross × (1 − 30% Steam cut) × 0.93 refunds]; Froke/Pretty Soon split unknown.
production_cost: ~$72k opportunity cost [ESTIMATE – 1 person × ~12 months × $6k/month (France lean-indie rate)] plus a 100-person closed playtest (no cost data); publisher Pretty Soon funded PR (Pirate PR campaign) – amount unknown.
development_time: ~1 year [CONFIRMED – dev's Reddit retrospective via Automaton 2026-08-25]
why_popular: Absurd, instantly readable premise: you are an intern who mass-produces rubber ducks and feeds them to a bottomless pit ('The Maw'), upgrading machines (magnets, fans, pistons, automatic makers) – an incremental/idle loop made physical, with thousands of ducks on screen (Kotaku: 'I tanked my framerate by making 100,000 rubber ducks'). Satisfying escalation, mystery ('ducking nightmare' job) and goofy physics are ideal YouTube let's-play content. Retro-styled presentation.
marketing_channels: Free itch.io version → big YouTube creators GrayStillPlays, ImCade, DangerouslyFunny (10M+ views per Pirate PR press release) → Steam page + demo → ~115k–120k wishlists at launch → publisher Pretty Soon with a Pirate PR campaign; launch discount; cross-bundle with 'Sort Them Ducks'; international press (Kotaku, TechTimes, Automaton x3, DLCompare, Steam Deck HQ).
engine: Godot [ESTIMATE – PCGamingWiki engine listing; no dev statement found]
art_style: Retro-styled 3D (Steam Deck HQ: 'ingenious retro sandbox'); rubber ducks, factory/'pit' facility, mass physics objects.
ai_feasibility_justification: AI can: write the incremental economy, upgrade trees, conveyor/machine logic, save system and UI; generate duck/prop models and retro textures, squeaky SFX and music; draft store copy. | AI cannot: make thousands of physics objects stay smooth (the game's main weakness – Kotaku hit 10 fps after ~5,000 ducks; Steam Deck drops to the 20s), balance idle pacing so it does not frustrate mid-game (the 'falling rubble' mechanic triggered backlash), pick representative playtesters, or win over YouTubers. | Toolset: Claude Code + Godot 4 (Jolt physics, MultiMesh instancing, object pooling/sleeping bodies) or Unity DOTS, Meshy/Tripo for props, Retro Diffusion/Scenario for textures/UI, ElevenLabs SFX, Suno music, GodotSteam.
solo_ai_mvp_cost_time: 3–6 weeks, ~$150–$500 (Claude Pro/Max, small 3D/audio subs; itch.io-first launch is free, $100 Steam Direct later). Excludes developer living costs.
solo_ai_polished_cost_time: 4–8 months, ~$2,000–$7,000 (subs, performance-optimisation work, capsule art, broad playtests, creator outreach/PR). Excludes developer living costs; a publisher may cover PR for a revenue share.

data_conflicts: Units/gross: dev 50k+ / $400k+ by Aug 24 vs Raijin ~22.3k / ~$187k – used dev data. Peak CCU: ~3,900 (dev) vs 3,928 (Raijin) – consistent. Reviews fell from 92% (launch day) to 78–80% within a week and stayed ~79%. Wishlists ~115k (press release) vs ~120k (dev via DLCompare/Automaton). Publisher: Pretty Soon (Steam/press) vs Plug-in Digital (Green Man Gaming listing, likely distributor). Release 08-19 vs 08-18 (Kotaku, time zone). Engine (Godot) comes only from PCGamingWiki. 'French' nationality comes from press descriptions, not a dev statement.
notes: Clear template for a solo creator: one absurd, visually escalating physics idea → free itch.io build → large YouTubers → ~120k wishlists → publisher-backed Steam launch, 50k copies in 5 days after ~1 year of solo Godot work. Cautionary lesson from the dev's own retrospective: a 100-person playtest of fans who already loved the demo missed mid-game pain points (the 'falling rubble' that broke player builds), and physics-object performance limits late-game scale; reviews dropped from 92% to ~79%.
